title: Tesana.ai - Game Dev online model/tool Review
author: Sirramza
selftext:
I wanted to leave my review after paying for the Max plan. And because there isn’t a lot of reviews about this tool.

  
I tried to create a Xcom like game but in The Expanse universe.



In short, I’m not happy with the tool for several reasons. Even setting aside the fact that my experience started with the tool bugging out, support suggesting that it might be because of the number of screenshots I uploaded, and then me realizing after a 30-second test that the actual issue was the links I had included in the prompt.



Even putting that aside — because I understand that, as an “early access” tool, there may be some minor issues — there are several other things that disappointed me.



I tested the same prompt I used in Tesana with Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT Astra Medium, Claude, and my local LLM. I have to say that Tesana’s game output was among the worst, alongside my local LLM. Its not bad, its just "mid" and "generic". The only area where I feel Tesana produced a good result — not excellent, but good — was with the 3D models it generated.



Then there’s the Max plan. Honestly, the name “Max” feels a bit scammy. Out of the 3,500 tokens included, around 2,500 were used up in just three prompts, and the result was still an extremely simple game. It doesn’t just feel like I get less usage than I do with ChatGPT; calling the plan “Max” also gives the impression that it is supposed to be a much more substantial plan, not something that can be exhausted in 30 minutes.



I understand that $20 can only get you so much, but getting less usage than what $20 gets you with ChatGPT is hard to justify.

  
It also spends tokens without necessarily producing the requested result. For example, when I asked it to create three variations of a character model, it made two actual variations, then copied a model it had already created earlier and simply gave it a new name. It claimed that this third version had certain characteristics, but it clearly didn’t, because it was literally just a copy of the previous model. The tokens were still consumed anyway.



Another thing I’d add, in one of my prompts, I pointed out that the characters were not showing the weapon models in their hands. Tesana told me that it had added them, but absolutely nothing was actually changed. The tokens were still consumed anyway.



Overall, I’m struggling to find any reason why Tesana is superior to the other tools currently available. And considering the price, the plan I tested — which, again, is called “Max” — feels more like a $20 demo than a proper paid plan.



I don’t want this to come across as an aggressive or angry comment. But compared to the impressions I got from YouTubers covering the tool, I came away disappointed after actually using it myself

  
Thinkin of asking a refund for the 1000 tokens i have left, not sure if it’s worth it or should i test one or two prompts more in the game.

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: I tried Tesana as well, but honestly, I think it's already outdated. Codex and Claude Code have advanced by leaps and bounds and direct platform costs are always preferable to an opaque credit system. Unity and Unreal both bundle MCP servers now, and Godot (which Tesana was using the last time I checked) has always been extremely LLM-friendly. In terms of bang for the buck, most times one is better served by a subscription on a code-capable frontier model plus MCP for any asset generation and engine integration one needs (with Codex naturally already shipping image generation).
